news.title: Protect your enterprise now from the Shai-Hulud worm and npm vulnerability in 6 actionable steps
news.summary_raw: Any development environment that installed or imported one of the 172 compromised npm or PyPI packages published since May 11 should be treated as potentially compromised. On affected developer workstations, the worm harvests credentials from over 100 file paths: AWS keys, SSH private keys, npm tokens, GitHub PATs, HashiCorp Vault tokens, Kubernetes service accounts, Docker configs, shell history, and cryptocurrency wallets. For the first time in a TeamPCP campaign, it targets password managers
news.summary: A worm, dubbed Shai-Hulud, targeting development environments by harvesting credentials from over 100 file paths has been discovered in compromised npm and PyPI packages. This poses a significant security risk that IT engineers must address immediately.
news.enterprise_use: Go to your AWS management console and immediately rotate any AWS keys associated with compromised developer workstations. Missing this step will leave your AWS environment vulnerable to data breaches. JumpCloud can help you track access and monitor user activity across all endpoints, but you must enable its MDM integration to enforce secure practices across your developer environment, which in turn will allow you to most effectively monitor and respond to this threat.
